title: I Reported the Fake Service Dog Jacket at the Grocery

parts.text: I watched a dog in a SERVICE vest lick the olive bar spoons. I am twenty-nine, ICU nurse off shift, unshockable, still tired. The vest was Amazon shiny, tags on. The owner, a man named Trent, filmed people who stared. My friend Nadia, sesame and now apparently olives, backed up. The store smelled like rotisserie and floor wax. Trent said, "It's a service animal, don't harass" I said, "Service dogs don't tour the olive bar" The manager, June, feared phones more than spoons. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is filming, the vest still has tags, and a spoon is wet.

parts.text: June arrived, looked at the tags, and asked the two questions stores are allowed. Trent refused and called it profiling. June asked him to leave the food bar area. He knocked a lemon into the ice. The dog, honestly, looked embarrassed, which is a projection. They left. June tossed the spoons. I bought Nadia sealed olives. Trent posted that the store hates veterans. He had not claimed a task until the parking lot. The store posted the actual policy. I still see shiny vests. I still look for tags. Tired nurses make good witnesses because we do not perform shock. June said, "What task is the dog trained to perform" Trent said, "Don't interrogate me" Nadia texted a photo of the sealed jar. That was the win. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i.
